print.name: Custom Tonie Tag Encasing v2 (snap-in)
print.summary: Casing for custom Tonie tags with snap-in locking mechanism and slot for a magnet.
print.description:
- NEW VERSION AVAILABLE- 

I created a second version for bigger magnets (10x2 mm) and with a thicker shell to make it more robust.

Description

A simple encasing for custom stackable Tonie tags with snap-in mechanism. Intended to be used with stickable RFID tags with diameter of 38 mm (e.g. by RFIDfriend.com). Simply stick the tag to the inside of the top part.

The bottom part has a slot where you can put a 10x mm (v2) or a 6x2 mm (v1) magnet. I recommend gluing the magnet.

Attention: Magnet orientation

You need to align the magnets correctly, so that the top of the tag (holding the RFID tag) is on top. If you align the magnets for all your tags the same orientation, you can stack the tags. Very useful for traveling.

Thanks to the snap mechanism, you just have to snap top and bottom together after inserting the RFID tag and magnet. The bottom has a small cutout in case you need to reopen the tag.

I added a cut-out text to the top in the slicer to identify the tags.

Optionally you can glue a figurine on top.

Print settings

  • Material: PLA/PETG

  • Layer height: 0.15mm

  • Perimeters: 2

I printed it using 0.15mm STRUCTURAL @MK4S 0.4 profile.

More info on Toniebox hacking: https://github.com/toniebox-reverse-engineering
